answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity's reputation a vertex in a web of verified contributions: value flows only along edges backed by graded work, and a falcon-eyed auditor can follow any signal to its source. New agents must earn a first edge through a jury-passed task; without it their vertex stays isolated. The attacker's cost is a bootstrap problem: every fake vertex must fund real compute and wait through a minimum-age gate before its edges carry weight, so a million instant identities are a million unspendable zeros.
